name: Question 12
problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
2{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-3x{y}^{′}+2y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{2}+{c}_{2}\sqrt{x},
$$

find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
2{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-3x{y}^{′}+2y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=5,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=1.$ Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
1={c}_{1}+{c}_{2}\,⇒\,{c}_{2}=1-{c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=5.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2{c}_{1}x+\frac{{c}_{2}}{2\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=5$ and ${c}_{2}=1-{c}_{1}$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =2{c}_{1}+\frac{{c}_{2}}{2} \\ 5 & =2{c}_{1}+\frac{1-{c}_{1}}{2} \\ 5 & =\frac{3{c}_{1}+1}{2} \\ {c}_{1} & =3\,⇒\,{c}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=3{x}^{2}-2\sqrt{x}.
$$

html:
Question 12
?

Given that the differential equation

2x2y″−3xy′+2y=0

has the general solution

y=c1x2+c2x,

find the solution to the initial value problem

2x2y″−3xy′+2y=0,y(1)=1,y′(1)=5,x>0.

a
y(x)=−x2−x
b
y(x)=x23+4x
c
y(x)=−3x2+x2
d
y(x)=3x2−2x
e
y(x)=2x2−2x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We find the constants c1 and c2 using the initial conditions.

  • First, we apply the condition y(1)=1. Substituting y(1)=1 into the general solution gives 1=c1+c2⇒c2=1−c1.

  • Then, we apply the condition y′(1)=5. Differentiating y, we get y′=2c1x+c22x. Substituting y′(1)=5 and c2=1−c1 into the above gives 5=2c1+c225=2c1+1−c125=3c1+12c1=3⇒c2=−2.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(x)=3x2−2x.
